transcript: Welcome to the 2024.2 new feature videos. In this video, we will look at the Go Z plugin improvements. You can download Go Z plugin for your operating system in the Go Z manual page by clicking Install Go Z in the Help tab on the main menu. Unzip the downloaded zip folder. Then you will get a packaged folder named Marvelous Designer. Move the packaged folder in the following directory. Run ZBrush. Go to Main Menu, Preference, Go Z, and click Path to Marvelous Designer. You will see the pop-up window displaying lists of different version of Marvelous Designer. Click the version's path you will be using. If a security warning window pops up, click Run. Once installation is done, run Marvelous Designer. Now you should see a Go Z tab in the Go Z menu. When exporting to ZBrush, go to Main Menu, Go Z, and click Export to ZBrush. The Exporting ZBrush window pops up and you will see that it's divided into two different areas. The Object area provides options to select and deselect avatars, patterns, trims, and scene and props to export. Unweld and Weld options is for whether you want your sewing lines to be unwelded or unwelded. You can also select which patterns to be detached or attached. You also have options for exporting thickness of your garments. In the Basic area, you could choose which scales you want your patterns to be exported. I will export. You could see how we have each item with different names in the subtool menu, and polygroups are automatically assigned. In the Import Go Z window, you have Load Type, Object Type, and Scale options. In Load Type, Object Type, and Scale options. In Load Type, Object Type, and Scale options. In Load Type, you have the option to select Open to import your items to a new project file, or Add to import your items into existing project file. The Object Type option has Avatar, Trim, Garment, and Scene and Props options. You are choosing whether you want to treat your object as an Avatar, Trim, Garment, or Scene and Props. Lastly, you have Scale options to choose which scale you want your avatar to be exported to. Here we import a character from ZBrush to Marvelous Designer. There is Go Z All and Visible buttons. I will click Go Z to simply export my character. Since we have set Object Type as Avatar, we are going to treat this character, Mesh, as an Avatar in Marvelous Designer. You can add Go Z for your character or use Go Z as a style. Here is the Go Z width, and the L width. Next we can animate our character to be represented in a model. Here we can add Go Z width to this character. You can add Go Z and Go Z width to different styles of characters. Or, you can add Go Z and Go Z together to a model. Choose and export your character. Here we have the size of an Avatar.
summary: # Marvelous Designer 2024.2: Goz Improvements ## Introduction Welcome to the 2024.2 new feature videos. In this video, we will look at the GoZ plugin improvements. ## Installation of GoZ Plugin You can download the GoZ plugin for your operating system from the GoZ manual page by clicking **Install GoZ** in the Help tab on the main menu. 1. **Download and Unzip**: Unzip the downloaded zip folder. You will get a packaged folder named **Marvelous Designer**. 2. **Move the Packaged Folder**: Move the packaged folder to the following directory. 3. **Run ZBrush**: Open ZBrush and go to **Main Menu > Preference > GoZ**. 4. **Set the Path**: Click **Path to Marvelous Designer**. A pop-up window will display a list of different versions of Marvelous Designer. Click the version's path you will be using. 5. **Security Warning**: If a security warning window pops up, click **Run**. 6. **Launch Marvelous Designer**: Once installation is complete, run Marvelous Designer. You should now see a **GoZ** tab in the GoZ menu. ## Exporting to ZBrush When exporting to ZBrush, follow these steps: 1. **Access Export Option**: Go to **Main Menu > GoZ** and click **Export to ZBrush**. 2. **Exporting ZBrush Window**: The Exporting ZBrush window pops up, divided into two different areas: - **Object Area**: Provides options to select and deselect avatars, patterns, trims, and scene props to export. - **Weld Options**: Choose whether you want your sewing lines to be unwelded or welded. You can select which patterns to detach or attach, and also have options for exporting the thickness of your garments. ### Basic Area Options In the Basic area, you can choose which scales you want your patterns to be exported. - **Export Preview**: You will see that each item has different names in the subtool menu, and polygroups are automatically assigned. ## Importing to Marvelous Designer In the **Import GoZ** window, you have several options: 1. **Load Type**: Choose between **Open** to import your items into a new project file or **Add** to import your items into an existing project file. 2. **Object Type**: Options include **Avatar**, **Trim**, **Garment**, and **Scene and Props**. You will choose whether to treat your object as an Avatar, Trim, Garment, or Scene and Props. 3. **Scale Options**: Select which scale you want your avatar to be exported to. ### Character Import Process Here we import a character from ZBrush to Marvelous Designer. There are **GoZ All** and **Visible** buttons. - I will click **GoZ** to simply export my character. Since we have set the Object Type as Avatar, we will treat this character mesh as an Avatar in Marvelous Designer. ## Character Animation and Styling You can add GoZ for your character or use GoZ as a style. - **GoZ Width**: Here is the GoZ width, and the L width. - **Character Animation**: Next, we can animate our character to be represented in a model. You can add GoZ width to this character and explore different styles. ### Exporting Character Size You can add GoZ and GoZ width to different styles of characters, or combine GoZ and GoZ together for a model. Choose and export your character. Here we have the size of an Avatar.
